summary: A confirmation dialog with a badge, title, description and a cancel/confirm pair, in two tones.

props.name: triggerIcon
props.description: A glyph beside the trigger's label.

props.name: triggerIconPosition
props.description: Which end of the trigger `triggerIcon` sits at.

props.name: triggerTone
props.description: The trigger's own colour, independent of the dialog's `tone` - a neutral button can still open a destructive dialog.

props.name: icon
props.description: The glyph in the badge above the title. No badge renders without one.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colours the badge and the confirm button together.

props.name: title
props.description: The dialog's heading, wired up by Base UI's own AlertDialog.Title.

props.name: description
props.example: This will remove Sarah from the team and revoke all project access.
props.description: The body text, wired up by Base UI's own AlertDialog.Description.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Called when the confirm button is pressed. The dialog closes either way.

props.name: showClose
props.description: The X in the corner. The Cancel button remains either way, so turning this off never traps anyone.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner radius on the popup, the badge and the buttons. `square` squares off the badge too.

props.name: animate
props.description: The backdrop's fade and the popup's scale-in. Turn it off for an instant dialog, or when the user has asked for reduced motion.

props.name: className
props.description: Appended to the trigger's classes, for anything the component leaves unset - a margin, `fs-0` in a flex row. It will not reliably override what the component already sets: which of two utilities wins is decided by the stylesheet's rule order, not by the order you write them.
